content:
Leah B: hey all, on day 1 and stuck on a couple of things. Okta SSO went through but Google Drive shows 'no access to this org'. also trying to register my YubiKey (USB-C + NFC) and Okta nags 'authenticator not recognized'. finally, 1Password desktop is signed in but the CLI `op signin` keeps giving state_mismatch. who should I ping?

Marie (IT): welcome Leah! can you paste the exact Google error? also are you using a personal laptop or company image? For the YubiKey, do you see a browser prompt to touch the key?

Leah B: message says: 'Your account is not provisioned for this product. Contact your administrator.' I'm on personal M1 MacBook. For the key, Chrome prompts then shows an orange error toast 'webauthn: unknown authenticator'. I do touch it when prompted.

Nora (People Ops): i triggered your account this morning at 09:05. Marie, could the provisioning worker have missed Drive app mapping? Leah, did you accept the invite link earlier?

Leah B: accepted at 09:12, got the welcome email.

Ben (Infra): quick checklist: 1) sign out of any existing Google accounts in the browser; 2) try the invite in an incognito window so it forces the SSO chooser; 3) for YubiKey, try Firefox if Chrome fails (different WebAuthn stack).

Marie (IT): checking the admin console now  looks like Drive license attached but the Google app mapping didn't apply due to a transient API rate error. i'll re-run the mapping and clear stale Okta sessions for leah.b@redwood.ai.

Leah B: tried incognito after a few mins, Gmail signed in but still no shared drives. Chrome still fails on the key. Firefox prompted and then showed a spinner before 'authenticator not recognized (0x6b)'. i swapped USB-C ports and then NFC worked when touching the key to the laptop's lid. odd but that registered the device.

Marie (IT): great, NFC touch sometimes triggers a different CTAP path that some YubiKey firmware handles better. i'll re-run the Drive mapping now. give it a minute and then refresh Drive.

Leah B: Drive appeared and i can see onboarding docs. thanks! one last piece: 1Password CLI. Desktop app is logged in, but `op signin redwood` in terminal errors with:
```
Browser returned error: 400 Bad Request
error_description: invalid_request: state_mismatch
Authentication failed: no active session
```
I tried closing the browser and re-running but same error.

Ben (Infra): 1Password CLI uses a local callback by default which can race if the desktop app or a previous browser session intercepts redirects. workaround: run `op whoami` to confirm desktop app session, then run `op signin redwood --raw` which prints a token. copy that token and run `eval $(op signin redwood --raw)` (or `op signin --session <NAME> <TOKEN>` depending on your CLI). That bypasses the local listener.

Marie (IT): also check for corporate VPN or hostname mappings; self-signed proxy certs can block the callback. Leah, are you on any VPN?

Leah B: not on VPN. ran the --raw flow and it worked. CLI env variables populated.

OnboardBot: Checklist update: Leah B completed "Google Workspace access", "MFA (YubiKey)", and "1Password CLI" at 2026-03-29 16:12 UTC.

Nora (People Ops): welcome to Redwood, Leah! i've added you to the eng Slack channel and the eng-dev GitHub team. DM me if you need anything else. :tada:
